# `cfb_toy_registry_2026` — cfbseedR 0.2.0 parity oracle

Designed cases for the season-scoped `CONFERENCE_TIEBREAKERS` registry and the
two CFP selection rules in `sportsdataverse/cfb/cfb_standings.py`. Unlike
`cfb_toy_tiebreakers/` (generated by Python), these expectations come from R:
`capture.R` writes the inputs, re-reads them and runs cfbseedR 0.2.0 over them,
so both engines consume the same CSVs.
`tests/cfb/test_cfb_standings.py::TestRegistry2026Parity` asserts Python
matches.

## Provenance

- Captured: 2026-11-02, R 4.5.3, cfbseedR 0.2.0 (`pkgload::load_all()` of the
  sibling `sdv-dev/cfbseedR` checkout at `28322e3`).
- Command, from the sdv-py repo root:

```sh
Rscript tests/fixtures/seedr/cfb_toy_registry_2026/capture.R ../cfbseedR
```

## Determinism

No case reaches a coin toss: every tie, including tail ties, resolves through a
games-based rung or a supplied rating. A re-capture that adds a case must keep
it that way (the Python and R RNGs differ).

## Cases (`case` column)

| Case | Conference | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `acc_2025` / `acc_2026` | ACC | Same games, season-keyed: 2025 uses the 2024 cascade (pooled opponents' win pct, A first), 2026 the new h2h -> analytics policy (B first). |
| `acc_pool_2026` | ACC | 2026 candidate pool: X (same wins as the leader) and Y (same losses) join the leader's tier; analytics then puts X 2nd over the better-pct Y. |
| `sunbelt_div` / `sunbelt_div_champ` | Sun Belt | `conf_division`: the two division champions take `conf_rank` 1-2; in `sunbelt_div_champ` the 1-2 West champion outranks the 2-1 East runner-up. |
| `sunbelt_div_pct` | Sun Belt | East's three 1-1 teams (E2-E3 never met) are split by `div_pct`: E2 is East champion, behind the 2-0 West champion W1. |
| `american_final_win` / `american_final_loss` | American Athletic | `cfp_ranked_final_week`: the ranked tied team advances after winning its final conference game, falls through to the composite after losing it. |
| `american_final_loss_nonconf` | American Athletic | As `american_final_loss` plus a later non-conference win: the clause reads the final *conference* game. |
| `cusa_apr` | Conference USA | Equal composite -> the `apr` rung decides. |
| `mw_composite` | Mountain West | The composite comes before head-to-head (B first although A beat B). |
| `mac_official` | MAC | MAC's three-step procedure: record vs common opponents ties, analytics decides (the old shared template would have ranked A first). |
| `ineligible` | Big Ten | `postseason_eligible = FALSE`: the 2-0 team drops behind every eligible team. |

## Files

- `games.csv`, `teams.csv` (optional `conf_division` / `postseason_eligible`
  columns, blank where a case does not use them — drop all-blank columns per
  case), `tiebreaker_data.csv` (`kind` = `analytics_ratings` / `cfp_rankings` /
  `apr`, one `value` column) — inputs, one block per `case`.
- `expected_standings.csv` — `case`, `team`, `conference`, `conf_rank`,
  `conf_champ` from `cfb_standings(games, teams, tiebreaker_data = ...)`.
- `seeds_standings.csv`, `seeds_rankings.csv` — a 16-team ranked field: P4
  champions T01, T02, T06 and T14 (ranked outside the top 12), Sun Belt champion
  T13 (the best G6 team), MAC champion T16, Notre Dame 12th.
- `expected_seeds.csv` — `cfb_playoff_seeds(..., autobid = "2025" | "2026")`;
  Python's `season=2025 | 2026`.

## Known divergences from cfbseedR 0.2.0 (kept out of the fixture)

- **G6 bid:** cfbseedR gives it to the best-ranked G6 *team*, champion or not;
  sdv-py to the best-ranked G6 *champion* (the CFP rule). The seeding fixture's
  best G6 team is a champion, so the engines agree on it.
- **Notre Dame:** cfbseedR reads the committee `rank` only and matches
  `"Notre Dame"` only; sdv-py reads Notre Dame's position in the ranking order
  (fallback order included) and also matches ESPN id `"87"`.
- **Season rules in standings / simulations:** cfbseedR's `cfb_standings()`
  always seeds with the 2026 rule and `cfb_simulations()` always uses the
  current registry; sdv-py follows a `season`-keyed input (or `season=`) for
  both. Every case here is a 2026 season or a direct `cfb_playoff_seeds` call.
- **ACC pool:** cfbseedR admits a team with no conference game (0-0) into an
  unbeaten leader's tier on matching its 0 losses; sdv-py requires at least
  one decided conference game. No case has a 0-0 team.
